title: Heavy-element (GeTe/SnSe) EXX blow-up localizes to single-atom-pair LRI fit error, not to NAO linear dependence
symptom: GeTe/SnSe EXX anomalies, extreme per atom pair: GeTe worst pair is atoms 2-4 at R = (0,0,0), distance 2.878 A, where an AO element has native S = -0.37249 but the fitted value is -0.81254; SnSe worst is atoms 3-3 at R = (0,-1,0), distance 4.285 A, where 0.18444 becomes 0.66670. Raising exx_cs_inv_thr to 1e-3 and 1e-2 clearly reduces the EXX anomaly but does not fix it. The huge EXX values (Ge 211 -> -9481 eV including a Q-direction -4150; Sn 153 -> -3206 eV including -2018) are reproduced by a wrong charge channel on top of a positive-semidefinite V, so they are not a PSD failure of the Coulomb matrix.
root_cause: Two effects are entangled: low eigenvalues of the AO overlap S(k) amplify the error, but the local (pair-wise) LRI fit matrix itself differs strongly from the global direct V for individual non-on-site atom pairs far apart. The audit conclusion is that the single-pair fit error is already large, so threshold sensitivity is a symptom rather than proof that the heavy-element NAO generation is bad.
minimal_fix: Localize per (atom pair, R): diff the LRI fitted block against the direct/full block and report the worst pairs with their distances, then investigate the fit for exactly those pairs (auxiliary-basis completeness / moment order) instead of tuning global inversion thresholds.
validation: Recompute the per-pair per-R block comparison table and require the worst element's relative error to drop once the pair-specific fit is improved; report exx_cs_inv_thr as a diagnostic that was varied, not as the fix.
avoid: Do not infer 'the NAO generation is bad' from threshold sensitivity, do not treat a PSD V or a good PBE band structure as proof that the LRI fit is good, and do not read the huge negative EXX energies as a PSD bug.
